findings.finding: Legacy MSTATUS_VM constants use pre-v1.10 draft encodings: MSTATUS_VM_SV39=9, MSTATUS_VM_SV48=10. The ratified SATP CSR uses SATP_MODE_SV39=8, SATP_MODE_SV48=9. This 1-off encoding mismatch is a footgun — if anyone mistakenly uses an MSTATUS_VM_* constant to program the satp CSR, the mode field will be wrong. The constants are currently unused (dead code), but their presence invites misuse.

SATP_MODE_SV39=8 and SATP_MODE_SV48=9 are correct per the ratified privileged spec. However, SATP_MODE_SV57 (=10) is missing despite MMU_SV57 being defined in cpu.h and parse_mmu_fdt recognizing 'riscv,sv57'. When SV57 support is added, a developer must remember to define SATP_MODE_SV57 = (10ULL << SATP_MODE_S). The omission is a normative gap that creates a latent integration hazard.

HENVCFG bitfield definitions are incomplete: PBMTE (bit 62) and STCE (bit 63) are defined, but ADUE (bit 61, Svadu extension) is missing. Only HENVCFG variants exist — MENVCFG_* and SENVCFG_* are entirely absent. On a non-hypervisor system, Svadu requires writing ADUE to senvcfg; without the constant, any future Svadu implementation would use a bare magic number. The privileged spec mandates SFENCE.VMA synchronization when toggling ADUE — the fence primitives exist (cpufunc.h:94) but cannot be correctly paired with a constant that doesn't exist.

MMU_SV39=0x1, MMU_SV48=0x2, MMU_SV57=0x4 as independent bitmask flags. The comment correctly documents the RISC-V privileged spec requirement that each level implies the previous (Sv48 ⇒ Sv39, Sv57 ⇒ Sv48 ⇒ Sv39). The bitmask design enables correct capability intersection across heterogeneous CPU clusters.

Address space layout documentation is accurate and comprehensive. Correctly enumerates all four page-based modes (SV32/SV39/SV48/SV57), honestly notes only SV39/SV48 are implemented, and provides correct VA boundaries for both implemented modes (256GB user for SV39, 128TB user for SV48). Kernel map layout is documented as identical across modes.
findings.snippet:
* RISC-V implements multiple paging modes with different virtual address space
 * sizes: SV32, SV39, SV48 and SV57.  Only SV39 and SV48 are supported by
 * FreeBSD.

findings.finding: VM_MAX_USER_ADDRESS_SV39=0x4000000000 (256GB) and SV48=0x8000000000 (128TB) are correct per the RISC-V spec for their respective modes. The compile-time default VM_MAX_USER_ADDRESS=VM_MAX_USER_ADDRESS_SV48 is safe because elf_machdep.c:122-135 dynamically selects the correct per-mode boundary at sysvec registration time, overriding USRSTACK/SHAREDPAGE/PS_STRINGS for SV39 hardware.

pmap_mode enum correctly represents the two implemented modes (SV39, SV48). VIRT_IS_VALID macro correctly selects the per-mode user-address boundary by testing pmap_mode at runtime. The design correctly gates SV48-only operations (e.g., pmap.c:408 KASSERT). SV57 is absent from the enum, consistent with the fact that it is not implemented.

Correctly implements the spec-mandated 'implies previous' rule: SV48 ⇒ SV39, SV57 ⇒ SV48|SV39. Default/unrecognized DT strings fall back to SV39-only, which is the minimum required for rv64 per the privileged spec. The unconditional MMU_SV39 baseline at line 341 ensures even CPUs with no mmu-type property get the mandatory base mode.

Global mmu_caps is correctly updated via intersection across all CPUs (update_global_capabilities, line 462: UPDATE_CAP(mmu_caps, desc->mmu_caps)). On CPU0, it's set directly; on subsequent CPUs, it's ANDed down. This ensures no MMU feature is advertised unless ALL harts support it, which is the conservative/correct approach for heterogeneous systems.

mmu_caps field in cpu_desc uses the same u_int type and MMU_SV* bitmask constants as the global mmu_caps, ensuring type consistency between per-CPU discovery and global aggregation. The field is populated by parse_mmu_fdt and consumed by update_global_capabilities — the data flow is clean.

Correctly bridges FreeBSD's internal pmap_mode enum to SATP CSR MODE field encodings: PMAP_MODE_SV39 → SATP_MODE_SV39=8, PMAP_MODE_SV48 → SATP_MODE_SV48=9. Values match the ratified RISC-V privileged spec. This is the sole translation point between the kernel's mode representation and hardware, so no mode-value inconsistency can leak through.

SFENCE.VMA inline function is correctly implemented with full memory clobber, providing both the architectural TLB invalidation and the compiler barrier needed for correct synchronization. The privileged spec requires SFENCE.VMA after writing ADUE to *envcfg CSRs; the fence primitive exists and is correct, though it is not yet called for this purpose since Svadu is unimplemented.

HFENCE.GVMA correctly implemented with full memory clobber. This is the hypervisor counterpart of SFENCE.VMA required for guest TLB invalidation when changing ADUE in henvcfg for virtualized guests. The infrastructure is in place for future Svadu virtualization support, even though the feature is not yet implemented.
